body:
Part of the E127 umbrella (#1183). Architect (2026-09-30): tokens are "not mandatory, but optional in all cases"; "if this for single repository, we can have only one token for all kinds of workloads"; without tokens, test on "a separate branch … with separate tree".

## Evidence (verified 2026-09-30)

- `.github/workflows/self-authored-pull-request.yml:58` already falls back: `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FORMAL_AI_BOT_TOKEN || github.token }}`, and `FORMAL_AI_BOT_TOKEN` is not configured (`gh secret list` shows no such repository secret).
- With the default token the bot pull request's checks wait for approval. GitHub's documentation (checked 2026-09-30): "When a pull request is created or updated by a workflow using `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `pull_request` events with the `opened`, `synchronize`, or `reopened` activity types create workflow runs that require approval."
- That is what happened to the bot pull requests: every check run on #1124 (7 workflows) has event `pull_request` with actor `konard`, i.e. they ran only after a person acted on the pull request.
- Three `pull_request` workflows cannot be dispatched at all: `layered-ci.yml`, `evidence-check.yml`, `workflows.yml` have no `workflow_dispatch` trigger.
- `release.yml`'s `workflow_dispatch` defaults to `release_mode: instant`, and several jobs run on any dispatch (`github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||` at lines 193, 263, 295, 383, 580), so dispatching it on a bot branch would take the release path.
- Upcoming workloads that open pull requests or issues: the daily dependency update (#1169), the parity document refresh (#1171), wrong-statement issues (#1179), cross-organization duplication issues (#1182), the self-coding ladder (#1170).

## Requirements

1. **R1 one resolver.** Every formal-ai workflow that writes to GitHub takes its token from link-foundation/.github `actions/resolve-github-token` (https://github.com/link-foundation/.github/issues/1): GitHub App (`AUTOMATION_APP_ID` + `AUTOMATION_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`) → one secret `AUTOMATION_TOKEN` → `github.token`. `FORMAL_AI_BOT_TOKEN` is replaced by `AUTOMATION_TOKEN` (the same name in every repository, so one organization secret or one GitHub App can serve all of them). No workflow skips or fails because a token is missing; the layer used is printed in the log and the job summary.
2. **R2 checks without approval.** When the resolver returns layer `default`, the workflow that opened or pushed the pull request runs link-foundation/.github `actions/dispatch-checks` for every `pull_request` workflow, so the checks start at once on the head commit. `layered-ci.yml`, `evidence-check.yml` and `workflows.yml` gain `workflow_dispatch` with the `mode: checks` input.
3. **R3 checks-only dispatch of `release.yml`.** A `mode` input (default `checks`) or a `checks` value for `release_mode` that is the default; every release, publish and tag job requires an explicit release mode **and** `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`.
4. **R4 isolation without tokens.** Workloads that need a separate test repository (the self-coding ladder's replayed tasks in #1170, any end-to-end test) use an orphan branch with its own tree in this repository (`e2e/<purpose>/<run_id>/<name>`, created with `git checkout --orphan` from only the files the test needs), an issue labelled `e2e-task`, and a pull request whose base is that branch; they close the issue and pull request and delete the branches at the end. A separate repository is used only when the resolver reports `can-create-repositories: true`. This repository's own `pull_request` workflows ignore `e2e/**` base branches (`branches-ignore`).
5. **R5 cross-repository work degrades, never fails.** A workload that files issues in other repositories (#1182's duplication findings, #1179 when a wrong statement belongs elsewhere) opens them directly with layer `app` or `token` when the credential can write there; with layer `default` it writes the findings to its report (`docs/status.md` and the case study) and keeps one tracking issue in this repository listing the issues to file.
6. **R6 documentation.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` gets a "GitHub credentials" section: the three layers, `AUTOMATION_TOKEN` as the only token name, the optional GitHub App, and that nothing needs configuring.

## Tests

- `rust/tests/unit/ci_cd/issue_1187_credentials.rs`: parses every workflow and composite action under `.github/`; fails when a workflow reads a GitHub-token secret other than `AUTOMATION_TOKEN` / `AUTOMATION_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, when a `pull_request` workflow lacks `workflow_dispatch`, or when a release job can run on `workflow_dispatch` without an explicit release mode and the `main` ref.
- Manual: with no `AUTOMATION_*` configured, label an issue `formal-ai-solve`; the bot pull request appears and all its checks start without approval (dispatch); the summary says `layer default`.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Requirement shard `docs/requirements/issue-1187-optional-github-credentials.md`; `rust-script scripts/assemble-requirements.rs --write`; traceability rows.
- [ ] Case study `docs/case-studies/issue-1187/` with the #1124 check history and the first bot pull request whose checks started by dispatch.
- [ ] Changelog fragment in `changelog.d/`; `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.98.1 rust-script scripts/run-ci-gates.rs --stage rust` green.

## Depends on / related

- https://github.com/link-foundation/.github/issues/1 (the shared actions).
- link-assistant/hive-mind#2323 and #2324 (the same rule in Hive Mind).
- Blocks the unattended runs of #1169, #1170, #1171, #1179, #1182.
title: E151: GitHub credentials optional in every workflow: one AUTOMATION_TOKEN (or GitHub App) for all workloads, dispatched checks for bot pull requests, orphan-branch isolation without tokens
